The #{00aaaa}ICF#{reset} can process different combinations of fuels at different laser power levels. A cheap and renewable fuel that can be used to gather the #{55ffff}Stellar Flux#{reset} needed for #{ffaa00}Gerald#{reset} and make decent power is #{55ffff}Helium-4 - Hydrogen#{reset}.

Applying a Muon Particle to a fuel pellet will decrease the power that is needed to run it.
ntnhcore.quest.76545.name: ICF Laser
ntnhcore.quest.76545.desc: #{00aa00}This quest provides an optional retrieval task for a small laser capable of running Helium-4 - Hydrogen Fuel at 15MHE.#{reset}
ntnhcore.quest.769.name: Pack configuration and optional modes
ntnhcore.quest.769.desc:
#{ffce86}Use the intended configuration#{reset}
Second Dawn has its own mod, recipe and config set. Arbitrarily enabling legacy HBM modes, removing mods or replacing configs can break quest dependencies and an existing world.

Legacy NTNH descriptions of Expensive, 528 and Rampant do not establish availability or compatibility in this Continuum build. This book does not recommend enabling them for normal progression.

Back up the full world and pack before changes and test a separate copy. Coordinate server changes with the administrator. Do not delete recipe folders to follow an old 1.7.10 instruction.
ntnhcore.quest.7681.name: Dairy Processing Tank
ntnhcore.quest.7681.desc: The #{00aaaa}Dairy Processing Tank#{reset}, while it can be crafted earlier, is very useful on Minmus because of the infinite #{55ffff}Milk#{reset} production from #{00aaaa}Pumps#{reset}. It can be used to process milk into different liquids, which can then be used to make food items.
ntnhcore.quest.76801.name: ICF Laser Turbocharger
ntnhcore.quest.76801.desc: The #{00aaaa}ICF Laser Turbocharger#{reset} can be placed next to #{00aaaa}ICF Laser Capacitors#{reset} to increase the laser's power by a substantial amount, allowing for the #{00aaaa}ICF#{reset} to run higher grade fuels.
ntnhcore.quest.77057.name: Magnetohydrodynamic Turbines
ntnhcore.quest.77057.desc:
#{00aaaa}Magnetohydrodynamic Turbines#{reset} are advanced components of the fusion reactor that make electricity out of the plasma energy directly without needing additional turbines. While more expensive and requiring #{55ffff}Perfluoromethyl#{reset} cooling, they have a #{ffff55}+35%#{reset} convertion bonus from #{ffff55}TU#{reset} to #{ffff55}HE#{reset}. In addition, the MDH turbine requires a minimum input of
#{ffff55}5MTU/t#{reset} of plasma energy to operate normally, otherwise efficiency will be halved.
ntnhcore.quest.77313.name: Murky Anvil
ntnhcore.quest.77313.desc: The#{00aaaa} Murky Anvil#{reset} is the ultimate version of the #{00aaaa}Anvil#{reset}, having all recipes unlocked.
ntnhcore.quest.77569.name: Osmiridium
ntnhcore.quest.77569.desc: #{ffaa00}Osmiridium#{reset} is the second most expensive material and is used primarely in the #{00aaaa}DFC#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.77825.name: Particle Accelerator
ntnhcore.quest.77825.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Particle Accelerator#{reset} is a highly modular machine that uses high strength superconducting magnets to accelerate particles to relativistic speeds in order to collide them together.

Due to the complex and expansive nature of the particle accelerator, it is highly recommend that the wiki is checked out as it provides more information.

[url]https://nucleartech.wiki/wiki/Particle_Accelerator[/url]

#{00aa00}This quest demands the most essential parts of the particle accelerator, and does not represent the amount needed for it to function.

#{ffce86}Legacy reference#{reset}
External wiki pages may describe another HBM version. Their structures, numbers and operating modes have not been verified against Continuum 1.20.1; compare them with the installed implementation. External site availability is not guaranteed.
ntnhcore.quest.78081.name: Particle Capsules
ntnhcore.quest.78081.desc: Particles are important items required to create exotic materials which are needed for most of the endgame content.
ntnhcore.quest.78337.name: Quantum Computer
ntnhcore.quest.78337.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Quantum Computer#{reset} is the most powerful out of any other control unit. It currently only used to build #{ffaa00}Gerald#{reset} and #{ffaa00}DFC#{reset}.

#{00aa00}A whole stack of them will be required, so now would be the time to upgrade circuit crafting infrastructure.
ntnhcore.quest.78593.name: Quantum Processing Unit
ntnhcore.quest.78593.desc: The #{ffaa00}Quantum Processing Unit#{reset} is the first quantum circuit one makes, used in the #{00aaaa}Particle Accelerator#{reset} and #{00aaaa}ICF#{reset} reactor.
ntnhcore.quest.78849.name: Schrabidium Hammer
ntnhcore.quest.78849.desc: The #{ffaa00}Schrabidium Hammer#{reset} is the most powerful weapon in the mod, being able to one-shot everything.
ntnhcore.quest.79105.name: Secret Catalogue
ntnhcore.quest.79105.desc:
In order to obtain a hidden catalog, you have to do a few things:

Get a regular sign
Answer the four questions and put the answers on said sign in the same order (all lowercase)
Right click the written sign
There will be answers with more characters than signs allow, just type out as many as possible.

There will be no hints, so don't even try it.
You'll need the bobmazon level 6 achievement to order anything.



1
When we scream into the distance, who will answer?

2
The invisible force, sometimes subtle and sometimes not, covers our eyes directed at the skies.

3
The fluorescent oscilloscope gives us the passcode of random numbers. Who holds the answers?

4
Ever revolving, never still, a sight for the patient that reeks of tobacco, dancing perpetually.
ntnhcore.quest.7937.name: Diesel Generator
ntnhcore.quest.7937.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Diesel Generator#{reset} is a compact, single-block generator that burns liquid fuels to produce energy. Its small footprint and compatibility with common oil-processing byproducts make it a strong choice for early- and mid-game power.

It holds up to #{55ffff}4,000 mB#{reset} of fluid internally, consumed at a steady rate of #{ffff55}20 mB/s#{reset}. It also carries a #{ffff55}50 kHE#{reset} energy buffer - but combustion does not pause when the buffer is full, so any excess energy is wasted. To avoid this, ensure your machines are drawing power consistently.

Fuel can be supplied via fluid ducts or by placing barrels in the internal item slots. A #{ffaa00}Fluid Identifier#{reset} can be inserted to lock the accepted fuel type. Not all fuels are equal - effectiveness varies by grade: medium-grade fuels run at #{ffff55}50%%#{reset} efficiency, high-grade at #{ffff55}75%#{reset}, and aviation fuels at just #{ffff55}10%#{reset}. Low-grade and gaseous fuels are rejected entirely.

#{00aa00}Tip: High-grade fuels like diesel, gasoline, and biofuel get the best return - prioritize refining your oil into these where possible.#{reset}
ntnhcore.quest.79361.name: Solid State Quantum Processor
ntnhcore.quest.79361.desc: The #{ffaa00}Solid State Quantum Processor#{reset} is the first quantum circuit related component needed to make #{ffaa00}Quantum Processing Units#{reset} and #{ffaa00}Quantum Computers#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.79617.name: Spark Laser Crystal
ntnhcore.quest.79617.desc: The #{ffaa00}Spark Laser Crystal#{reset} unlocks new recipes, most importantly it is used to create #{ffaa00}Osmiridium#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.79873.name: Spark Singularity
ntnhcore.quest.79873.desc: The #{ffaa00}Spark Singularity#{reset} is a singularity made from combining all the types of singularities with #{ffaa00}Dineutronium#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.80129.name: The Book of Boxcars
ntnhcore.quest.80129.desc: The #{ffaa00}Book of Boxcars#{reset} is an item which allows the crafting of many special items. The book can be found inside #{ffff55}Meteorite Dungeons#{reset} found randomly in the wilderness on extra-terrestial bodies, indicated by a black pillar, or in #{ffff55}Red Rooms#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.80385.name: The Crucible
ntnhcore.quest.80385.desc: The #{ffaa00}Crucible#{reset} is a weapon that deals extreme amount of damage. It can be recharged inside a Tungsten Crate shot by a #{00aaaa}DFC Emitter#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.80641.name: The Digamma Particle
ntnhcore.quest.80641.desc:
The #{ff5555}#{reset}#{aa0000}#{reset}#{ffaa00}Digamma Particle#{reset} is created by colliding a #{ffaa00}Sparkticle Capsule#{reset} with a #{ffaa00}Higgs Boson Capsule#{reset} in a #{00aaaa}Particle Accelerator#{reset}. Making it in the particle accelerator will require #{ffaa00}Chlorophyte Coils#{reset} and momentum of 70,000.

The digamma particle emits a different kind of radiation, #{aa0000}DRX#{reset}, which currently can only be countered by the use of digamma medication, most notably #{ffaa00}Enteramine Pills#{reset}, which provide full immunity against DRX for 10 minutes. After the #{00aaaa}DFC#{reset}, Fau armor can be crafted which provides full resistance against DRX.
ntnhcore.quest.80897.name: UFO
ntnhcore.quest.80897.desc:
The Martian Invasion Ship is a late-game boss which is killed to get the #{ffaa00}UFO Coin#{reset}, used in crafting Gerald.

This quest provides an alternative way of obtaining the coin.

#{00aa00}This quest can be repeated.
ntnhcore.quest.81153.name: Welded Osmiridium Plate
ntnhcore.quest.81153.desc: #{ffaa00}Welded Osmiridium Plates#{reset} cost 300 Billion #{ffff55}HE#{reset} to produce, so good energy generation and storage infrastructure is needed.
ntnhcore.quest.81409.name: Yharonite Billet
ntnhcore.quest.81409.desc: The #{ffaa00}Yharonite Billet#{reset} is created in a tungsten crate that has #{ffaa00}Polonium Billets#{reset} in it while being shot from a #{00aaaa}DFC Emitter#{reset}. This is the final material obtained in the mod.
ntnhcore.quest.81665.name: Acceleration Card
ntnhcore.quest.81665.desc: The #{ffaa00}Acceleration Card#{reset} increases the speed of various AE2 devices.
ntnhcore.quest.8193.name: Do a Barrel!
ntnhcore.quest.8193.desc:
#{00aaaa}Barrels#{reset} are storage blocks that can hold both fluids and solid blocks. Wooden barrels will leak liquids over time and burn down if filled with lava, so use a stone barrel for those recipes.

Barrels placed under open sky will collect rainwater during downfall.

When filled with organic material, a barrel will begin composting once completely full. After roughly 100 seconds it produces a dirt block, ejected by right-clicking. Dirt left near mycelium will slowly convert into a mycelium block, no Silk Touch needed.

A wooden barrel filled with #{55ffff}Water#{reset} placed next to cobblestone will slowly convert it into mossy cobblestone, costing #{ffff55}100 mB#{reset} per block. The surrounding blocks must be unaffected by rain. Placing a barrel on mycelium converts its water into #{aa00aa}Witch Water#{reset}, though the barrel itself may disappear in the process. Water flowing above a barrel filled with lava transforms into obsidian.

Stone barrels can spawn creatures when tapped with a doll: a barrel of lava with an Angry Doll summons a Blaze, and a barrel of #{aa00aa}Witch Water#{reset} with a Creepy Doll summons an Enderman.

Barrels can convert items using fluids: #{aa00aa}Witch Water#{reset} turns sand into soul sand, lava turns redstone into netherrack or glowstone dust into end stone, and #{55ffff}Water#{reset} can turn dust into clay, milk into slime balls, or mushroom stew into #{aa00aa}Witch Water#{reset}.

#{00aa00}Hoppers can be used to insert and eject items from barrels, making composting easy to automate.#{reset}
ntnhcore.quest.81921.name: AE2 Autocrafting
ntnhcore.quest.81921.desc:
#{00aa00}This quest serves an a guide on how to order items using the ME system. The example item will be an Analog Circuit.#{reset}

With an #{00aaaa}ME Drive#{reset} providing item storage, a #{00aaaa}Crafting CPU#{reset} and #{00aaaa}Interfaces#{reset}, one can request any item to be crafted. The image below makes use of a #{00aaaa}Molecular Assembler#{reset}, a #{00aaaa}Soldering Station#{reset}, an #{00aaaa}Electric Press#{reset} aswell as two #{00aaaa}Import Buses#{reset} which serve as an output for the solderer and press.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_Auto1.png[/img]

The first step in automating crafting recipes is to encode #{ffaa00}ME Patterns#{reset}. There are two types of patterns, crafting and processing. The crafting pattern is created by having the #{00aaaa}Pattern Terminal#{reset} set to the crafting table. After placing the items in the terminal, press the arrow to finish encoding the recipe.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_Auto2.png[/img]

For recipes which arent made in a crafting table, such as the #{ffaa00}Wires#{reset} and the #{ffaa00}Analog Circuit#{reset} itself, the pattern terminal needs to be switched to the processing mode, which has a furnace icon.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_Auto3.png[/img]

After all the patterns have been created, insert them into their respective interfaces.
Make sure to enable blocking mode on the interfaces as not to have multiple different recipes enter the interface at once.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_Auto4.png[/img]

Finally, after everything has been set up, the option to order items will be shown in the ME terminal.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_Auto5.png[/img]
ntnhcore.quest.82177.name: AE2 in Second Dawn
ntnhcore.quest.82177.desc:
#{ffce86}Modern AE2 with recipe adaptations#{reset}
Applied Energistics 2 for Minecraft 1.20.1 and compatible add-ons are installed. Selected recipes and legacy features are adapted through NTNHCore for HBM progression.

An old AE2 wiki is not an exact description of this pack. Check item, meteorite or machine availability in the current world and JEI. Some legacy add-on features remain unported; an entry in the book does not make them available.

ExtendedAE and Glodium support the adapted wireless branch. Check each device's quest and Known Issues for its limitations.
ntnhcore.quest.82433.name: Cable Fluix
ntnhcore.quest.82433.desc:
The #{ffaa00}ME Glass Cable - Fluix#{reset} is a cable used to transmit data and energy between devices in an ME Network. It is capable of transmitting #{ffffff}#{ffff55}8 channels#{reset} simultaneously.

The #{ffaa00}Quartz Fiber#{reset} is used to transfer energy, but not channels.

#{ffaa00}Cable Anchors#{reset} can be used to seperate ME cable connections. They can also be used to make #{ffaa00}Facades#{reset} for the cables.
ntnhcore.quest.82689.name: Cell Workbench
ntnhcore.quest.82689.desc: The #{00aaaa}Cell Workbench#{reset} allow to filter cells to accept specific items. It can prove useful for when making a subnet for #{ffff55}Bedrock Ore Processing#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.82945.name: Certus Quartz Crystal
ntnhcore.quest.82945.desc:
#{ffaa00}Certus Quartz#{reset} is an important material in AE2. It is dropped when mining or processing certus quartz ore at the rate of one to four, the yield is affected by a tool's Fortune enchantment. Certus Quartz is often interchangeable with vanilla #{ffaa00}Nether Quartz#{reset} in the recipes for basic tools, such as the #{ffaa00}Quartz Cutting Knife#{reset}. Certus quartz ore can be acidized or centrifuged for an increased yield.

#{00aa00}Certus quartz can later be made in a Chemical Plant using nether quartz.
ntnhcore.quest.83201.name: Charger
ntnhcore.quest.83201.desc: The #{00aaaa}Charger#{reset} is a machine which will charge #{ffaa00}Certus Quartz Crystals#{reset} into their charged form at the expense of power.
ntnhcore.quest.83457.name: Crafting CPU
ntnhcore.quest.83457.desc: The Crafting CPU is a multiblock structure composed of #{00aaaa}Crafting Co-Processing Units#{reset} and #{00aaaa}Crafting Storage#{reset}. When placed next to eachother they form one CPU which is used when placing orders via #{00aaaa}Interfaces#{reset}. The more crafting co-processing units the more tasks the CPU can do in parallel while more crafting storage allows for bigger orders to be made.
ntnhcore.quest.83713.name: Crystal Growth Accelerator
ntnhcore.quest.83713.desc: The #{00aaaa}Crystal Growth Accelerator#{reset} is a machine that uses energy to accelerate the process of crystal purification. This process transforms crystal seeds into pure versions of their fully developed counterparts.
ntnhcore.quest.83969.name: Crystal Growth Chamber
ntnhcore.quest.83969.desc:
The#{00aaaa} Crystal Growth Chamber#{reset} is a machine in which crystals can grow at an increased speed, while also being in a block instead of being dropped in the ground.

#{ff5555}Some objectives still need to be ported. Unsupported objectives are blocked; see the pack report.
ntnhcore.quest.84225.name: Dense ME Cable
ntnhcore.quest.84225.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Dense ME Fluix Cables#{reset} can be used to transmit #{ffff55}32 channels#{reset} from an #{00aaaa}ME Controller#{reset}.

One controller is capable of connecting up to 6 dense cables, in turn each can branch off to 4 smaller cable lines connecting up to 192 ME devices to the network.

The #{ffaa00}Smart Dense Cable#{reset} also displays the amount of channels that are been used, but is known to be less performance friendly than the dense covered cables.

In addition there are 16 colored cables made with the appropriate dye. The colored cables allow contact with other cables without sharing the signal or connecting to any other cable but the ones of the same colour.
ntnhcore.quest.8449.name: Dosimeter
ntnhcore.quest.8449.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Dosimeter#{reset} is an tool for detecting radiation and assessing radioactive contamination.

It is functionally similar to a #{ffaa00}Geiger Counter#{reset}, but it collects much less data - only the general radiation contamination of the environment. Only a handheld version of the dosimeter is available. To obtain radiation information, right-click while holding the dosimeter.

Like a counter, it makes a characteristic crackling sound when radiation is detected.

#{00aa00}The maximum radiation displayed is 3.6 RAD/S.

Not great, not terrible.
ntnhcore.quest.84481.name: Energy Acceptor
ntnhcore.quest.84481.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Energy Acceptor#{reset} transfers energy into the ME system. In combination with an #{00aaaa}HE to RF Converter#{reset}, the ME system can be powered.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_EnergyAcceptor.png[/img]
ntnhcore.quest.84737.name: Energy Cell
ntnhcore.quest.84737.desc: The #{00aaaa}Energy Cell#{reset} acts as a battery for the ME network. It becomes useful when the ME system begins to consume large amounts of energy, so a buffer is needed so it doesnt turn on and off constantly.
ntnhcore.quest.84993.name: Fluix Crystal
ntnhcore.quest.84993.desc:
#{ffaa00}Fluix Crystals#{reset} are another crystal type which is used in crafting recipes throughout the mod. The crystal comes in two forms, the regular fluix crystal and the #{ffaa00}Pure Fluix Crystal#{reset}.

To create a fluix crystal, 1#{ffaa00} Charged Certus Quartz#{reset}, 1 #{ffaa00}Nether Quartz#{reset}, and 1 #{ffaa00}Redstone Dust#{reset} must be dropped into a pool of #{55ffff}Water#{reset}. They will be consumed and output 2 fluix crystals.

#{00aa00}Fluix crystals can later be made in a Chemical Plant using charged certus quartz and redstone.
ntnhcore.quest.85249.name: Infinity Booster Card
ntnhcore.quest.85249.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Infinity Booster Card#{reset} allows one to access their ME system across any distance and dimension. To apply simply open the #{ffaa00}Wireless Crafting Terminal#{reset} and insert the card in it.

#{ff5555}Some objectives still need to be ported. Unsupported objectives are blocked; see the pack report.
ntnhcore.quest.85505.name: Interface P2P
ntnhcore.quest.85505.desc:
The #{00aaaa}P2P Interface#{reset} is a P2P device which can be used to easily paralellize recipes across many machines.

#{ff5555}Some objectives still need to be ported. Unsupported objectives are blocked; see the pack report.
ntnhcore.quest.85761.name: ME Buses
ntnhcore.quest.85761.desc:
The #{00aaaa}ME Export Bus#{reset} is an ME component which is used to export items from the ME network into a machine or other input inventory. 

The #{00aaaa}ME Import Bus#{reset} is an ME component which is used to import items directly into the ME Network from a machine or other output inventory.

#{00aa00}It is recommended that Interfaces are used over Export/Import buses for performance reasons.
ntnhcore.quest.86017.name: ME Controller
ntnhcore.quest.86017.desc: The ME Controller acts as the routing hub of an ME network. It can support up to 8 devices connected to it.
ntnhcore.quest.86273.name: ME Drive
ntnhcore.quest.86273.desc: The #{00aaaa}ME Drive#{reset} serves as the storage of the ME system, in which #{ffaa00}Storage Cells#{reset} can be put and store items.
ntnhcore.quest.86529.name: ME Interface
ntnhcore.quest.86529.desc: The #{00aaaa}ME Interface#{reset} is a block which allows the ME Network to interact with machines and inventories. On their own, they can be used to automatically stock inventories, but can be used with #{ffaa00}ME Patterns#{reset} later on for autocrafting.
ntnhcore.quest.86785.name: ME IO Port
ntnhcore.quest.86785.desc: The #{00aaaa}ME IO Port#{reset} can transfer the contents of storage cells into an ME Network and back.
ntnhcore.quest.8705.name: Drainage Pipe
ntnhcore.quest.8705.desc: The #{00aaaa}Drainage Pipe#{reset} allows the dumping of fluids and gasses into the environment at the cost of pollution.
ntnhcore.quest.87041.name: ME Pattern
ntnhcore.quest.87041.desc: #{ffaa00}ME Patterns#{reset} are used to encode recipes to be used in #{00aaaa}Interfaces#{reset}. They can be encoded in a #{00aaaa}Pattern Terminal#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.87297.name: ME Storage Bus
ntnhcore.quest.87297.desc: The #{00aaaa}ME Storage Bus#{reset}, when attached to an block/tile entity with an inventory (generally a storage unit, such as chests or a #{00aaaa}Drawer Controller#{reset}), will include that inventory's contents in the ME System.
ntnhcore.quest.87553.name: ME subnetting
ntnhcore.quest.87553.desc:
#{ffff55}Subnetworks#{reset} are ME networks which can be accessed from a #{ffff55}Main Network#{reset}. In #{ff55ff}NTM#{reset}#{reset} they can be useful for storing items from passive processes without flooding the main storage network.

#{00aa00}This quest serves as a guide on how to set up a subnet, which can be used to store the resourses that Bedrock Ore Processing produces.#{reset}

In the image below are two ME networks, the #{ff5555}Red#{reset} one as the #{ff5555}Mainnet#{reset}, and the #{5555ff}Blue#{reset} one as the #{5555ff}Subnet#{reset}.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_NET1.png[/img]

For the purposes of this quest, the main network will store dirt blocks, while the subnet will store copper blocks.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_NET2.png[/img]

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_NET3.png[/img]

To make the contents of the subnet, the copper blocks, visible to the main net, one must make an #{00aaaa}Interface#{reset}-#{00aaaa}Storage Bus#{reset}#{reset} combo. The storage bus must be on the side of the main network.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_NET4.png[/img]

Make sure to filter the main network storage bus, and to also make it "Extract Only".

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_NET5.png[/img]

Now the main network has access to materials stored on the sub network, which can be used for crafting.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/BQ_NET6.png[/img]
ntnhcore.quest.87809.name: ME Terminal
ntnhcore.quest.87809.desc: The #{00aaaa}ME Terminal#{reset} is used to access all available items in the ME Network, including craftable ones.
ntnhcore.quest.88065.name: Modifier Cards
ntnhcore.quest.88065.desc: #{ffaa00}Modifier Cards#{reset} allow for modification to various ME components, such as speeding them up or being able to toggle them on and off using redstone.
ntnhcore.quest.88321.name: Molecular Assembler
ntnhcore.quest.88321.desc: The #{00aaaa}Molecular Assembler#{reset} is used to autocraft anything that can be made in a crafting table.
ntnhcore.quest.88577.name: Network Tool
ntnhcore.quest.88577.desc: The #{ffaa00}Network Tool#{reset}, when right-clicking on any network device will bring up the tool's interface showing all devices connected to the network as well as network details. As any wrench, shift clicking on a cable will remove it.
ntnhcore.quest.88833.name: Network Visualisation Tool
ntnhcore.quest.88833.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Network Visualisation Tool#{reset} is used to visuallize an ME Network by right-clicking on any of its blocks, making it very useful when making a large network, especially one that uses #{00aaaa}P2P#{reset}.

#{ff5555}Some objectives still need to be ported. Unsupported objectives are blocked; see the pack report.
ntnhcore.quest.89089.name: Overflow Void Card
ntnhcore.quest.89089.desc: The #{ffaa00}Overflow Void Card#{reset} acts as a voiding upgrade for AE2 #{ffaa00}Storage Cells#{reset}. It can be added to a storage cell using the #{00aaaa}Cell Workbench#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.89345.name: P2P
ntnhcore.quest.89345.desc:
#{ffaa00}P2P#{reset} Tunnel or "Point to Point Tunnels" are a versatile configurable system to move items / redstone / power / and fluids from one location to another though an existing ME Network without storage.

Tunnels are #{ffff55}1 input to N outputs#{reset}. This means you can output to as many points as you want, but only input at a single point per tunnel.

Networks can support any number of tunnels, of any different types, and they all function independently.

ME tunnels can be used to carry channels from one location to another, and can carry up to #{ffff55}32 channels#{reset}, same as a #{ffaa00}ME Dense Cable#{reset}, while only requiring a single channel per point, making tunnels a very powerful tool to expand me networks, especially over a distance. However with the great flex-ability they give you comes a limitation, the channel of a p2p tunnel cannot be carried by another p2p tunnel, meaning that you cannot nest them recursively.

To configure a P2P tunnel you must first attune the tunnel to carry what you want it to, then you need to configure the outputs to their input. You configure the connections by using the #{ffaa00}Memory Card#{reset}. First Shift+Right Click the input to save it on your memory card, then simply right click the different outputs to store the input onto the outputs. this also sets the type of the output to match the type of the input.

#{00aa00}An advanced version of the Memory Card can also be made, which interacts with the entire network.
ntnhcore.quest.8961.name: Space: preparation first
ntnhcore.quest.89601.name: P2P Interface Parallelisation
ntnhcore.quest.89601.desc:
Parallelisation of processes can significantly cut down on waiting time and as such it is highly recommended that P2P Interfaces are used.

#{00aa00}This quest serves as a guide on how to use P2P Interfaces.#{reset}

As any P2P Connection goes, there needs to be one input, which in this case, holds the #{ffaa00}ME Patterns#{reset}.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_P2P_Interface1.png[/img]

After patterns are inserted in the first P2P interface, place down the rest of the output interfaces you want and link them together using a #{ffaa00}Memory Card#{reset}.

In the image below, the P2P interface highlighted in green stores the patterns, while the ones in blue, are the output ones which will connect machines to the ME system.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_P2P_Interface2.png[/img]

Make sure to have blocking mode enabled on all output P2P interfaces as to prevent clogging and having multiple recipes trying to be executed at once in the same machine.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_P2P_Interface3.png[/img]

Finally, place your desired machines at the output P2P interfaces and add a way of retrieving the items once the operation is done, in this case import buses.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_P2P_Interface4.png[/img]
ntnhcore.quest.89857.name: P2P ME Networking
ntnhcore.quest.89857.desc:
#{00aaaa}P2P ME#{reset} can be used to transport massive amounts of channels without laying many cables.

#{00aa00}This quest serves as a guide on how to effectively use P2P ME.#{reset}

Once an #{00aaaa}Energy Acceptor#{reset} has been set up, it is highly recommended (and likely needed) that an #{00aaaa}Energy Cell#{reset} is placed next to it as to ensure that there is enough power going to the system, as more components increase the energy demands of the ME system.

After that, 2 #{00aaaa}ME Controllers#{reset} are required, one to provide the channels that machines will use, and another to transport the other's channels by the P2P connections. The top controller can be made bigger by attaching more controllers next to it.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Controller1.png[/img]

After the controllers are placed, on the top controller, a P2P Tunnel - ME needs to be placed on any side. The #{5555ff}Blue Cable#{reset} will serve as the cable that connects the P2P connections, and as such, it needs to be connected to the bottom controller.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Controller2.png[/img]

By linking the P2P connections together using a #{ffaa00}Memory Card#{reset}, the 32 channels from one side of the top controller will only use 1 channel from the bottom controller to be transported to any destination. The #{ff5555}Red Cable#{reset} now has access to 32 channels.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Controller3.png[/img]

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Controller4.png[/img]

By expanding on the previous example, more connections can be added to fully utilize all channels.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Controller5.png[/img]

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_controller6.png[/img]
ntnhcore.quest.90113.name: Pattern Capacity Card
ntnhcore.quest.90113.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Pattern Capacity Card#{reset} can be used to add 9 more slots for patterns in an #{00aaaa}ME Interface#{reset}. Up to 3 cards can be inserted.

#{ff5555}Some objectives still need to be ported. Unsupported objectives are blocked; see the pack report.
ntnhcore.quest.90369.name: Quantum Network Bridge
ntnhcore.quest.90369.desc:
A #{00aaaa}Quantum Network Bridge#{reset} is a multiblock structure that connects 2 potentially distant, or even in different dimensions, network fragments together. Created by crafting 8 #{00aaaa}ME Quantum Ring#{reset} and a #{00aaaa}ME Quantum Link Chamber#{reset} and placing the ME quantum link chamber in the center, and sourrounding it in the 8 ME quantum rings.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Qring1.png[/img]

Each quantum network bridge requires power to function. This power must be provided from the network fragment it is attached to until the bridge is linked; at which time power from either side will be available. However if power is lost, connectivity will fail and power will be drained from the side the bridge is on in attempt to restore connection.

To establish a link between 2 quantum network bridges, you must create a pair of #{ffaa00}Quantum Entangled Singularities#{reset}. One of each will be placed inside of a particular connection. Each Bridge may only connect to one other bridge.

[img height=1000]betterquesting:textures/QB_Qring2.png[/img]

AE2 Singularities are created by dumping 256k of any block inside a #{00aaaa}Matter Condenser#{reset}. Singularities can become quantum entangled by dropping a singularity and ender dust and then exploding them together.
ntnhcore.quest.90625.name: Spatial IO
ntnhcore.quest.90625.desc:
#{00aaaa}Spatial IO#{reset} is a way to cut-and-paste physical volumes of space in your world. It works by swapping the defined volume with an identically-sized volume in the spatial storage dimension, sending whatever's in the pylon array to the spatial storage dimension, and whatever's in the dimension to the pylon array.

Spatial IO requires a specific arrangement of its components in order to function, and define the volume to be cut-and-pasted. All of the components must be on the same network in order to function, and you can have only one spatial IO setup on a network. Thus, a subnetwork is recommended.

The #{00aaaa}Spatial IO Port#{reset} controls the spatial IO operation. It shows stats on the multiblock setup, and holds the spatial cells

To perform a spatial IO operation, place a #{ffaa00}Spatial Storage Cell#{reset} in the input slot and give the spatial IO port a redstone pulse. It will then swap the volume in the pylons with the volume in the spatial storage dimension. This means that if you send some set of blocks to the spatial storage dimension, then put another set of blocks in the pylons, put the cell back in the input slot, and trigger the IO port again, the 2nd set of blocks will disappear and the 1st set of blcks will reappear.

Any entity in the defined volume, including you, will be carried along, and if you have no way of getting out, you will be trapped in the spatial storage dimension.

#{00aaaa}Spatial Pylons#{reset} are the main part of a spatial IO setup, and define the volume to be affected. The volume is defined by the bounding box of the outside of the pylons, contracted in by 1 block in all directions.
ntnhcore.quest.90881.name: Storage Components
ntnhcore.quest.90881.desc: The #{ffaa00}ME Storage Housing#{reset} is the outer shell of a #{ffaa00}Storage Cell#{reset}. There are many tiers of storage cells, all of which require the use of NTM machines to be crafted.
ntnhcore.quest.91137.name: Wireless Connectors
ntnhcore.quest.91137.desc:
#{00aaaa}Wireless Connectors#{reset} allow for channel linking without ME cables, making it possible to send channels through walls. The further away the connectors are the more energy consuming they become.

A #{00aaaa}Wireless Hub#{reset} can be used to link channels between multiple wireless connectors.
ntnhcore.quest.91393.name: Wireless Crafting Terminal
ntnhcore.quest.91393.desc: An upgraded version of the #{ffaa00}Wireless Terminal#{reset}, capable of crafting items on the go.
ntnhcore.quest.91649.name: Wireless Terminal
ntnhcore.quest.91649.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Security Terminal#{reset} can be used to specify what players are allowed to interact with in the ME network which can be useful in multiplayer. It can also be used to link a #{ffaa00}Wireless Terminal#{reset} to the ME network. Atleast one #{00aaaa}Wireless Access Point#{reset} is required, and its range can be expanded using #{ffaa00}Wireless Boosters#{reset}.

#{ff5555}Some objectives still need to be ported. Unsupported objectives are blocked; see the pack report.
ntnhcore.quest.91905.name: ArchitectureCraft
ntnhcore.quest.91905.desc:
#{ff55ff}ArchitectureCraft#{reset} introduces the #{00aaaa}Architect's Workbench#{reset} which can be used to change the shapes blocks.

The #{ffaa00}Architect's Hammer#{reset} can be used to easily rotate the blocks.

The #{ffaa00}Architect's Glowbrush#{reset} can be used to apply light to any block.
ntnhcore.quest.9217.name: Electric Furnace
ntnhcore.quest.9217.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Electric Furnace#{reset} is a furnace that is powered by electricity. it is slightly faster than the vanilla furnace without upgrades. it consumes from #{ffff55}1 kHE/s#{reset} without upgrades up to #{ffff55}4 kHE/s#{reset}.

Due to it only being slightly faster than the vanilla furnace, it isn't used much beyond early game, but it can be used in automation, if speed isn't the main objective.
ntnhcore.quest.92161.name: Auto Chisel
ntnhcore.quest.92161.desc: The #{00aaaa}Auto Chisel#{reset} allows for automated chiseling of blocks. Simply insert any chisel in the machine and the block that will act as the template.
ntnhcore.quest.92417.name: Better Builder's Wands
ntnhcore.quest.92417.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Building Wand#{reset} allows one to place many blocks at once, making walls and roads easier to construct. The stronger material the wand is made out of, the more blocks it can place.

#{00aa00}To replace water blocks using wands bind the key, Change Fluid Mode, in settings.
ntnhcore.quest.92673.name: Building Gadget
ntnhcore.quest.92673.desc:
The #{ffaa00}Building Gadget#{reset} is an advanced building tool which allows the user to create many complex shapes with ease. Press the ALT key to open its menu.

#{00aa00}It consumes power for blocks placed.#{reset}
ntnhcore.quest.92929.name: Chisel
ntnhcore.quest.92929.desc: The #{ffaa00}Chisel#{reset} is a building tool which can be used to change the textures of blocks, and even unlock new and unique designs.
ntnhcore.quest.93185.name: Modern Markings
ntnhcore.quest.93185.desc: #{ff55ff}Modern Markings#{reset} adds wall and floor decorations suited for many purposes. Use the #{ffaa00}Chisel#{reset} on the floor or wall signs to change their design.
ntnhcore.quest.93441.name: Schematica
ntnhcore.quest.93441.desc: With #{ff55ff}Schematica#{reset}, you can create schematics of your builds and post holograms of them on other worlds. Check out the keybinds to get started.
ntnhcore.quest.93697.name: Sign Pictures
ntnhcore.quest.93697.desc: The #{ff55ff}SignPicture#{reset} mod allows one to put any image on a sign, opening the door to many unique building designs. Press \ to get started.
ntnhcore.quest.93953.name: Farming and AgriCraft
ntnhcore.quest.94209.name: Food and dietary variety
ntnhcore.quest.94465.name: Balls-O-Tron
ntnhcore.quest.94465.desc: Balls-O-Tron is the second boss of NTM. It can be summoned by interracting the Mechanist's circle, found in the Enargite Temple which spawns in jungles, with a Silver Key, made using the Maskman Coin.
ntnhcore.quest.9473.name: Power and network compatibility
ntnhcore.quest.9473.desc:
#{ffce86}Different power systems#{reset}
HBM uses HE; other installed mods may display FE or their own units. Similar-looking cables or energy names do not guarantee compatibility.

Check each machine's inputs, outputs, voltage and limits. The adaptation includes selected energy devices and converters, but the book does not promise a universal exchange ratio or compatibility with every block.

Test a small source-storage-consumer chain first. Confirm transfer direction and buffering before expanding. Old NTNH numerical tables are not verified parameters for Continuum 1.20.1.
ntnhcore.quest.94721.name: Martian Invasion Ship
ntnhcore.quest.94721.desc:
The Martian Invasion Ship is a late-game boss which is killed to get the UFO Coin, used in crafting Gerald.

It can be summoned by crafting the Martian Invasion Ship item.
ntnhcore.quest.94977.name: #{aa0000}MEGAKILL!
ntnhcore.quest.95233.name: Time to Kill (Blaze)
ntnhcore.quest.95233.desc: You should be careful with this task. Fire protection is highly recommended. [warn]Blazes are always spawning infernal.[/warn]
ntnhcore.quest.95489.name: Time to Kill (Chicken)
ntnhcore.quest.95489.desc: Screaming doesn't help. You're going in the soup.
ntnhcore.quest.95745.name: Time to Kill (Cow)
ntnhcore.quest.95745.desc: I think I need a new backpack. Let's slaughter a few cows.
ntnhcore.quest.96001.name: Time to Kill (Creeper)
ntnhcore.quest.96001.desc:
Who hasn't experienced this... You're just minding your own business, mining a few diamonds, and suddenly, you wake up in your bed, all your items gone. 

Time to strike back!
ntnhcore.quest.96257.name: Time to Kill (Enderman)
ntnhcore.quest.96257.desc: Uh, fancy teleport pearls. You need them. All of them. Now!
ntnhcore.quest.96513.name: Time to Kill (Ghast)
ntnhcore.quest.96513.desc: They shoot you with explosive fireballs but they are weak when you hit them or knock the fireballs back with a weapon. Better upgrade your armor with fire and blast protection.
ntnhcore.quest.96769.name: Time to Kill (Magma Cube)
ntnhcore.quest.96769.desc: Now a Hell version of your slime!
ntnhcore.quest.97025.name: Time to Kill (Pig)
ntnhcore.quest.97025.desc: Mmm... turn on the grill. We need more meat.
ntnhcore.quest.9729.name: Energy Cables
ntnhcore.quest.9729.desc:
The most basic block for transmission is the #{00aaaa}Red Copper Cable#{reset}, which comes in two varieties, a block form and a skinnier cable form. The block form also has a paintable version which can help it blend into your designs better.

For better looking, as well as longer distance energy transportation, a #{reset}#{ffaa00}Cable Drum#{reset} with #{00aaaa}Electricity Connectors#{reset} can be used. These powerlines are non solid and can also pass through floors and walls.
ntnhcore.quest.97281.name: Time to Kill (Pigman)
ntnhcore.quest.97281.desc: "Zombie Pigman"? What the hell is going on with you zombies?! Maybe you should encase your animals better at night...
ntnhcore.quest.97537.name: Time to Kill (Sheep)
ntnhcore.quest.97537.desc: Oh no, not the poor sheep! Fluffy and red, I'm so sad.
ntnhcore.quest.97793.name: Time to Kill (Silverfish)
ntnhcore.quest.97793.desc: Be wary, they like to disguise and clone themselves in stone-related blocks! (Applies to Vanilla blocks only) Can be found within dungeons and hills. Can also be found in Drowning Creeper spawned cobblestone blocks.
ntnhcore.quest.98049.name: Time to Kill (Skeleton)
ntnhcore.quest.98049.desc: Arrows are nice, if you shoot them. If one hits you, well, bad things happen.
ntnhcore.quest.98305.name: Time to Kill (Slime)
ntnhcore.quest.98305.desc: Sticky and bouncy! Now in many variations. Say hello to my little friend, Lemon Slice!
ntnhcore.quest.98561.name: Time to Kill (Spiders)
ntnhcore.quest.98561.desc: Eeeek! Wall climbing monsters, gross! Slay them. Quickly! Watch out for the witch spiders, they can give as good as they get.
ntnhcore.quest.98817.name: Time to Kill (Squid)
ntnhcore.quest.98817.desc: Delicious squid. We're making Tom Yum seafood.
ntnhcore.quest.99073.name: Time to Kill (Witch)
ntnhcore.quest.99073.desc: Witches bring stitches because they are always infernal and very dangerous. Be careful since they throw potions at you.
ntnhcore.quest.99329.name: Time to Kill (Wither)
ntnhcore.quest.99329.desc: After collecting a couple of those wither skeleton heads, you feel like you could use some more action. So why not kill a wither?
ntnhcore.quest.99585.name: Time to Kill (Wither Skeleton)
ntnhcore.quest.99585.desc:
Gimme yo Skuuuuull!!!#{reset} <-- The thought of every non-noob player upon seeing one.

BTW, in case you didn't know, you can summon the Wither by placing 4 soul sand blocks in a T shape, with 3 wither skulls on top. Don't do so in your base.
ntnhcore.quest.9985.name: Flare Stack
ntnhcore.quest.9985.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Flare Stack#{reset} is a generator that produces energy by burning flammable liquids and gases. Any fluid tagged as Flammable can serve as fuel - supply it through pipes or directly via containers.

Operation uses three steps. First, fill the internal buffer (capacity: #{ffff55}64,000 mB#{reset}) with fuel. Second, open the #{ffaa00}Flow Valve#{reset} at the top of the middle section to release fuel from the buffer into the combustion system. Third, enable the #{ffaa00}Ignition#{reset} switch at the bottom of the middle section to ignite the fuel and begin power generation.

Efficiency is low: gases burn at #{ffff55}50%#{reset} and liquids at only #{ffff55}10%#{reset}. Output also varies by fuel type.

Two upgrades are available: the #{ffaa00}Speed Upgrade#{reset} increases throughput, and the #{ffaa00}Effectiveness Upgrade#{reset} improves fuel efficiency.
ntnhcore.quest.99841.name: Time to Kill (Zombie)
ntnhcore.quest.99841.desc: Nobody knows who they are, or where they came from. They're just annoying at night, and too stupid to make a crafting table.
ntnhcore.quest.100097.name: Maskman
ntnhcore.quest.100097.desc: Maskman is the first NTM boss. To summon it, you need to be under radiation poisoning (50 rad). A 20-minute timer starts per player when requirements are met. Once it runs out, Mask Man spawns. A warning appears 1 minute before spawn. If you are no longer irradiated, the timer resets.
ntnhcore.quest.100353.name: Card Base
ntnhcore.quest.100609.name: Component Buses
ntnhcore.quest.100865.name: Computer
ntnhcore.quest.101121.name: Computer Casings
ntnhcore.quest.101377.name: Control and Arithmetics Units

ntnhcore.quest.102145.name: Floppy Disks and Disk Drive
ntnhcore.quest.102145.desc:
The #{00aaaa}Disk Drive#{reset} can be used to read #{ffaa00}Floppy Disks#{reset} using a computer connected to it.

This is useful to get started, since the lower tier #{00aaaa}Computer Cases#{reset} do not have a built-in floppy slot, and you'll need an operating system to boot up the computer.
ntnhcore.quest.1025.name: Air Intake
ntnhcore.quest.1025.desc: The #{00aaaa}Air Intake#{reset}, when powered, produces #{55ffff}Compressed Air#{reset} needed in #{00aaaa}Pneumatic Pipes#{reset} and #{55ffff}Hot Air Blast#{reset}.
ntnhcore.quest.10241.name: Flint Tools
ntnhcore.quest.10241.desc:
#{ffaa00}Flint Tools#{reset} are required to obtain first wood and stone. Break some tree leaves and get saplings, to recraft them into sticks.

Axes automatically break tree blocks from top to bottom to prevent floating trees. Hold Shift to disable this and break blocks normally.

Only the flint pickaxe and hatchet are required. The flint shovel is optional. Logs require an axe; leaves can be broken by hand to obtain saplings for sticks.
ntnhcore.quest.102401.name: Graphics Cards
ntnhcore.quest.102657.name: Hard Drives

ntnhcore.quest.104449.name: Servers
